variants.title: Potentiometer: a Leclanché cell against a Weston standard cell
variants.unknown: the emf of the standard cell from the two balancing lengths
variants.note: The Weston cadmium cell is the laboratory standard of emf: 1.01865 V at 20 degrees Celsius. It must never be asked for more than a microampere, which is why a potentiometer, drawing no current at balance, is the only proper way to measure it.

source.title: Weston cadmium standard cell: 1.01865 V at 20 degrees Celsius (international standard of electromotive force)

variants.title: Potentiometer: a Leclanché cell against a lead-acid cell
variants.unknown: the emf of the lead-acid cell
variants.note: A single lead-acid cell gives about 2 V, more than the Leclanche cell, so this time the second balancing length is the longer one.

source.title: NCERT Physics Textbook Class XII, Chapter 3: a secondary (lead-acid) cell has an emf of about 2 V

variants.title: Potentiometer: a Leclanché cell against a nickel-cadmium cell
variants.unknown: the emf of the nickel-cadmium cell
variants.note: A nickel-cadmium cell is sold as a 1.2 V cell, against the 1.5 V of a dry Leclanche cell: the potentiometer shows that difference as a difference of balancing lengths.

source.title: Nickel-cadmium secondary cell: nominal cell voltage 1.2 V (IEC 61951-1 cell designation)
